findings.summary: Spec item 4's owner-side durable action-key dedup is absent on the production DD path. DdOwnerSource.resume accepts action_key and discards it; DdControlPlane.gate has no action-key parameter and no persistent (action_key, generation) unique constraint, only a transient STATE_RUNNING liveness check. The systemd unit passes no --owner-url, so cli.py:553 leaves owner_url None and DdOwnerSource is the production owner. Failure: intent_recorded persisted, gate() launches the resume, SIGKILL before the terminal seal; on restart _complete_intent (bridge.py:287) re-calls resume, gate() finds the development no longer STATE_RUNNING with a checkpoint present, and _launch(resume=True) performs a second real recovery for the same decision -- precisely the double-apply item 4 exists to prevent. decision_bridge/__init__.py:32-36 states the substitution explicitly, crediting the bridge's own receipts unique index (store.py:67) as 'owner-side' dedup.

Exactly-once is regression-verified only against a fake in-memory owner, so it cannot catch the finding above. Both acceptance scenarios drive the bridge via --owner-url at FakeOwnerState, whose dedup is an in-process set(). The unit tests likewise inject a fake OwnerSource, and test_action_key_is_a_unique_constraint (tests/test_decision_bridge.py:158) exercises the bridge's receipts index rather than any owner-side constraint. The spec's 验收 requirement for kill-restart-exactly-once therefore passes without ever exercising the production DD resume path.

The line resume owner named by spec item 4 ('DD 与 line 恢复拥有者') and by the boundary constraint requiring line recovery through a registered controlled entry restricted to the waiting generation is entirely unimplemented. OWNER_KIND_LINE is declared (owners.py:35) and the resolver carries line handling (WAITING_LINE_STATE at resolver.py:36, the kind!='dd' branch of _stale_reason at resolver.py:184), but no LineOwnerSource class exists, no production owner source can discover or resume a line target, and no test covers the path. Lines fall back entirely to the 60s poller.

The cursor can advance past a decision that never reached a terminal disposition, violating spec item 1's 'cursor 只在事件获得终态 disposition 后推进'. seal_terminal writes board_seq = excluded.board_seq unconditionally (store.py:311), unlike advance_cursor which uses MAX (store.py:190). In run_once's message loop (bridge.py:176-181), a message that hits failed_closed:receipt_unreadable (bridge.py:222-229, e.g. a 'database is locked' exceeding the 3s busy_timeout) returns without advancing, but the loop continues; a later message in the same page that seals successfully then sets the cursor to its own higher seq, permanently skipping the unprocessed decision. Bounded by the preserved 60s GateAutoResumer fallback, so the decision degrades to slow recovery rather than being lost outright.

run_once is documented 'Never raises; returns what it did' (bridge.py:144) and the module docstring claims 'Every failure is a recorded fact, never a crash' (bridge.py:17-21), but BridgeStoreError raised by record_intent or seal_terminal inside _process_message is not caught by the message loop and escapes run_once and run_forever, terminating the process. With Restart=on-failure this becomes a crash-loop instead of the documented recorded-fact degradation. The end state is still zero resume, so this is a contract/robustness gap rather than a safety hole.

On the production path a control-plane read failure during discovery is indistinguishable from a genuine no-owner decision, and seals a terminal no-op that advances the cursor. DdOwnerSource.discover swallows every exception and returns [] (owners.py:96-103), so resolve_decision's discovery_errors branch (resolver.py:137-153) is dead code for DD: during a control-plane outage the receipt reason reads only 'no waiting owner references this question', losing the distinction the structured-reason requirement of spec item 3 is meant to preserve.

The committed implement handoff records work_head_commit as af64fe0e16c6bcc809e658b41154d79b7215c25c, while the dispatch context for this review states the product commit (work_head_commit) is a755450cacacae7e6176d691cce34f8e4f2c28a6. The context additionally asserts work_head_commit equals implementation_subject_commit, which is inconsistent with the described materializer behaviour of stacking a metadata-only commit on top of the product commit. Flagged for the Engine to reconcile; it does not affect the verdict, which rests on spec conformance of the tree.

The mechanical product-equality check between a755450c and 44dea2ce (git diff --exit-code excluding .dev-dispatch) was NOT performed: this reviewer has only read-only file inspection, and shell access in this session is confined to the run workdir and cannot reach the worktree. No claim is made either way about metadata-only materialization; the review covers the worktree tree contents as read. This is disclosed rather than assumed, and does not change the REJECT, which stands on the spec-conformance findings above.
